extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current Harvard GSAS graduate students (PhD and master's) seeking information about financial support
extracted.subtask_description: Informational overview of Harvard GSAS financial support: the school's commitment to financial accessibility, available resources/links, and contact details for the Office of Financial Aid. Meant to direct students to aid services and related policy pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim: financial accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Our aim is to attract the most qualified candidates and make Harvard financially accessible to all degree candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level institutional commitment indicating admissions and funding decisions should support access; no scoring or procedural details provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Financial Aid assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you are a PhD student or studying for a master’s degree, the dedicated staff of the Office of Financial Aid can help you develop a plan that enables you to secure the resources you need to pursue your graduate education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises students to work with the Office of Financial Aid for individualized planning; contact via gsasfinaid@fas.harvard.edu or phone 617-495-5396 (address also provided). Specific programs, eligibility criteria, and application steps are on linked pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences does not discriminate against applicants or students on the basis of race, color, national origin, ancestry or any other protected classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms equal treatment in admissions and financial support; no further procedural detail on complaint or enforcement processes on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked financial resources and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages linked from this section include: Cost of Attendance 2026–2027; Cost of Attendance 2025–2026; Find Your Financial Aid Officer; Funding and Aid; Regulations Regarding Employment; Financial Wellness; Consumer Information; Taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These linked pages are the substantive sources for program eligibility, amounts, employment regulations, and other financial policies — the current page serves as an index/portal rather than a detailed rubric. Users should follow specific links for criteria, deadlines, and application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact details for seeking aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial Aid — Richard A. and Susan F. Smith Campus Center, 1350 Massachusetts Avenue, Suite 350, Cambridge, MA 02138-3654; Email gsasfinaid@fas.harvard.edu; Phone 617-495-5396.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides means to initiate individualized financial-aid conversations; recommended action for students seeking specific funding guidance or clarifications not found on linked pages.
